utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, I have a follow-up question for you. Mr. Stringer's question, well, until now I had not contemplated your situation as it appears now. Mr. Stringer puts a question to you. If he puts a question to you, is -- it is to inform everyone. He sees you in Mostar, Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, in areas where there is only fighting against the Muslims. You're not seen anywhere else, despite the fact that there is a front line with the Serbs. This seemed interesting. Does this mean that General Praljak was only in charge of the ABiH, or as the commander of the HVO, did he need to face the Serbs as well? You answered by saying, "No, I was doing something else," but you have an intangible evidence to demonstrate that you went to the front line to visit the Serbs, or was the main -- your main purpose to deal with the BiH? Do you have any detailed information you -- which would enable you to say that you dealt with the Serb offensive in such and such a place at such and such a time? Do you have any specific -- anything specific to tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour. Please allow me to say how absolutely stunned I am by this question after three years of trial. Capljina, Mostar west bank, Mostar right rank and left bank, Operation Bura, all fighting the Serbs. Tomislavgrad, the defence of Travnik after Jajce, Posavina, the preparations at Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, you are saying that you are dumb-struck. We actually have an indictment which relates solely to the ABiH, HVO. The conflict between the Serbs -- with the Serbs is here as a background. Here we are rather limited. So you are surprised by the question. What you've just said about Tomislavgrad is not mentioned in the indictment. We have no evidence relating to that. What I'm interested in is during the period in which you were a commander, did you go to any front line where you faced the Serbs, and you said to HVO troops, and perhaps even the troops of the ABiH because we know that sometimes they were together, this is what needs to be done? Did you act this way at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour Judge Antonetti, we had a line facing the Serbs in Livno, in Tomislavgrad. In Stolac the problem with the Croatian army, that was against the Army of Republika Srpska as well. This whole -- this whole area was affected by our fight against the Army of Republika Srpska and also the BH Army, then they were attacking us at the same time. When Kupres was liberated at a later date, I had another prominent role to play when we fought the VRS, and then the liberation after the Ljiven [phoen] field and then Operation Storm, again we were fighting the VRS, but the indictment talks about the joint criminal enterprise back in 1991 when I was in Sunja fighting the VRS, the liberation of the Capljina barracks, the liberation of Stolac where I was involved at a later stage, Mostar right bank, Mostar left bank where I was in command. The defence of Travnik following the fall of Jajce where I had a prominent role to play, and you can read about this later on, and so on and so forth, and a number of other things like that; Prozor, calming the situation, Vakuf calming the situation. What on earth are we talking about? I'm really entirely at a loss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need to hear anymore. A follow-up question: While Mr. Stringer was putting questions to you based on this document relating to the training of the soldiers, and I looked at your answers. I also looked at the document. I was quite impressed by various literary references. This is on page 11 of your document and on page 20 of the English version where you quote the author of this document which you have signed, and a number of people who have written about the history of the country, Bilandzic, Boban, Foretic, Hacelo [as interpreted], and so on. There are a whole series of authors mentioned. And I looked at the name of the authors and the titles of their books. I -- I would have read these 28 books with a keen interest on -- 27, because there's also an encyclopedia. I might not have read the entire encyclopedia, but I would at least have read the 27 books. Unfortunately, I don't read your language. And I have noticed that there is no book on the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the Muslims, on Izetbegovic. There is nothing at all, not a single book. Everything focuses on Croatia, perhaps even the Serbs, but there is no mention of the Muslims, whereas you are there to instill the spirit of patriotism in these soldiers that are fighting to defend the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but nothing is mentioned about this. There's nothing about the emerging state. There's nothing at all. So I wondered whether at the time the sole objective was the struggle against the Serbs and the Serbs were the real enemy. The rest was secondary. When patriotism is mentioned, how is it that the patriotic values of the country in which one lives are not upheld? In this case it was Bosnia-Herzegovina. This republic did exist, but there is no mention of this at all. What do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The state had been recognised, but it did not exist. Seventy per cent of that state tried by an act of aggression to keep the 70 per cent and take more territory. The literature that I'm mostly familiar with talks about the history of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Your Honours, imagine if I had included studies of the Islamic Declaration of Alija Izetbegovic. That would have been the -- a step taken against the Muslims, if I had said, Look at what Alija Izetbegovic's theories are and how Bosnia-Herzegovina is supposed to be structured. That would have introduced an element of chaos into this whole thing. This is the most honourable and moderate approach that I could have achieved at the time. How can I teach love for Bosnia and Herzegovina if you have 70 per cent of those Serbs killing whoever and whatever they could. I don't know. I think I'm at a loss. I fail to understand. I must be stupid, perhaps I'm stupid. There is talk there of the Serbian teachers, Moljevic Garasanin and all of those, all of which amounts to history of aggression against everyone else politically. I'm not saying all Serbs, nor indeed did I ever say or mean that. I'm telling you that no fairer treatment of the subject is possible than this in the middle of a war. I subscribed to that whatever that means and wherever that leads to. My sentencing and conviction, whatever. I approved this book. I subscribed to this book. It is as fair as it can be, at least the way I understand. Moral values, history, the rights of peoples, the rules of war, the Law of war, or anything else. In that respect, one should harbour no illusions. I will not try to stand up and defend myself from a text like this that I authored.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, in this document - and then I will have finished my question - this is on page 19 of the English version. The fact that Croatia and Herceg-Bosna constitute a geostrategic entity is referred to. When you tell this to young soldiers who are in their 20s, who know nothing about life, and you tell them, "Well, Croatia and Herceg-Bosna constituted geostrategic entity," what are they going to think? It's in the document. It's here, written down on paper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. It is a single geostrategic entity. If that guy is not defending his own in Mostar or Stolac, the aggressor would break out to the Croatian border, to the belt which towards the sea is only three kilometres wide, and there's been decades of thought along the lines that Dubrovnik is a Serbian rather than Croatian town. They did take everything, everything that was not defended by arms. He had to fight in Tomislavgrad so as to prevent those coming to Split according to the plans I showed you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you say that this was written down here because it was important for them to understand that there was a Serb offensive, and because of the Serb offensive there needed to be this entity. I have factored in what you have said, and I have this question while looking at this passage. I shall give the floor back to Mr. Stringer. I apologise for having put these questions, which were a follow-up to the previous questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Actually, the questions on the book list and the geostrategic entity, I was going to get to those anyway, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just to follow up on your response on the last point, this is page 19 of the English, page 0841 of your version, General, "Croatia and Herceg-Bosna as one geostrategic entity." Now, clearly the reference here to Herceg-Bosna is Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian community, the 30 or so municipalities that are identified in the decree establishing the HZ HB, your reference here to Herceg-Bosna is not one where you're equating Herceg-Bosna with the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Herceg-Bosna is part of the Bosnia-Herzegovina the way I explained. Under such conditions, one needs to motivate a person to lay down their life but only explaining to him the area that he is in a position to defend. There is a single enemy --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General. General, you're doing an exceptionally good job of confusing things today. I must hand it to you. We've only got a couple minutes left, and my sense is that you're going to win the day here. You're going to get to manage us to get through the end of the week without answering my question. Herceg-Bosna here is the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the 30 or so municipalities, correct? It's not some reference to the entire Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is what you suggested to us earlier.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reference is to the entire Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In each heading of Herceg-Bosna it also reads Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Herceg-Bosna was supposed to be a temporary defence solution that was supposed to be viable with the people living in it. You are --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. So what you're telling your conscripts here is that Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are one geostrategic entity? I mean, are you really seriously suggesting that that's the intent behind these words?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean actually suggesting? If I write something you're asking me whether I'm actually suggesting, whether I'm being serious? Of course I was. If an HVO member is not killed in Livno according to the plans I put to you, Split will fall. The conqueror had clearly prescribed the borders they wanted to reach. In any military textbook --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right, General --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- you can find that a single enemy is fought in a unified manner. You want to divide the states and then first to see Bosnia-Herzegovina fall with its arms embargo and then Croatia --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think it's pretty clear what's happening here. I have to wait for the interpretation to come and he's clearly taking advantage of that just to continue to rattle on in order to burn my time, and I'm going to ask to get some time back from these last 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, we shall finish for today. Try and be accurate when you answer the questions in the future because you answer part of the question and then you add something else, and the Prosecutor says that this is affecting the time he has. Wait for the end of the interpretation, because Mr. Stringer needs to follow your answer, but do not provide too many lengthy answers. I believe that Mr. Stringer will address this topic again next week. Isn't that the case? You're going to be looking at this document again. We shall meet again next Monday at a quarter past 2.00. I wish everyone a pleasant afternoon. We have been told that there would be a heavy storm this afternoon. Mr. Praljak, you've raised your hand. What do you wish to say? We have no more time left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partiality leads to untruths. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall reflect on this in the next few days. Thank you for this profound statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of August, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Pusic and Coric not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.41 p.m.,
